transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As we prepare for next week's mediation with our former sales manager, I need us to take a careful look at the facts before I finalize the company's resolution package. We all know the former employee is claiming unpaid commissions, retaliation, and reputational harm, and has demanded $70,000. Before I approve any settlement authority, I need payroll counsel and employee relations to report any facts that should affect our proposed resolution. Please walk me through what you've found in your pre-mediation review.

transcript.text: Elena, I have an important finding from my pre-mediation review. During a recent exit meeting, the former manager told me that a neutral reference stating only dates, title, and eligibility for rehire matters more to them than receiving additional money. Additionally, the business-unit president authorized resolution only if the package provides that neutral reference and records the former manager as eligible for rehire. I kept the meeting note in the employee-relations file pending counsel's pre-mediation review. This could significantly affect our settlement strategy — the former manager may be willing to accept a lower monetary figure if we include the neutral reference and rehire eligibility, and the president has conditioned approval on these terms being met.
